blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
The pandemic changed how we think about work. In a few weeks, millions of employees went remote — and many of them never went back to the old model. Today, hybrid work is the norm for knowledge workers in most countries.

Designing a hybrid policy is harder than it sounds. How many days in the office? Fixed or flexible? Which roles can go fully remote? What about people in different time zones? And how do you keep culture and informal connections alive when the team is rarely together?

If the pandemic hadn't happened, many companies would still be debating whether remote work was possible. Now we know it is — and the real question is how to make it fair, productive and humane.

items.q: According to the text, what is hybrid work today?
options: The norm for knowledge workers in most countries
items.why: "hybrid work is the norm for knowledge workers in most countries".

items.q: Why is designing a hybrid policy "harder than it sounds"?
options: Because employees refuse to work from home
Because many trade-offs — days, roles, time zones, culture — must be balanced
items.why: O 2º parágrafo lista várias perguntas difíceis: dias, papéis, fusos, cultura.

items.q: What does the sentence "If the pandemic hadn't happened, many companies would still be debating…" suggest?
options: The pandemic settled a question that was previously unresolved
The debate has not changed at all
items.why: Inferência: a pandemia forçou uma resposta que antes seria apenas discutida.

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: Remote work has proven to be possible
A single hybrid rule fits every role equally well
items.why: Inferência: o texto pergunta "which roles can go fully remote?", implicando que nem todo papel serve à mesma regra.

items.q: The phrase "fair, productive and humane" suggests the author believes a good policy should…
options: serve people as well as performance
items.why: Inferência: "humane" e "fair" mostram preocupação com as pessoas, não só com resultado.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Harry conduzindo o workshop sobre políticas híbridas. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Right, let's get into it. I'm going to put three hybrid models on the board, and I want each of you to tell me which one your team could actually live with.

Model one is fixed days — everyone in on Tuesday and Wednesday, no exceptions. It's simple, and it guarantees in-person time, but it ignores people's real lives and their commutes. Model two is fully flexible — come in whenever you like. People love it in the survey, but honestly, the office ends up empty and the informal interaction we say we value just disappears. Model three is what I'd call anchored flexibility: two required days a month for collaboration, and the rest is yours.

Here's my honest view. If we had rolled out fully flexible last year without any anchor days, I think the team would have drifted apart completely. We very nearly did. So my advice is: protect a little in-person time on purpose, but don't turn attendance into the goal. And please, set boundaries — if people are always on because they're remote, we haven't given them flexibility, we've taken their evenings.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What does Harry ask the managers to do?
options: Report how many people are in the office today
Say which of three models their team could actually live with
Design a brand-new model from scratch
items.why: "tell me which one your team could actually live with".

items.q: What problem does Harry see with the fully flexible model?
options: It forces everyone in on the same days
People hated it in the survey
The office empties out and informal interaction disappears
items.why: "the office ends up empty and the informal interaction we say we value just disappears".

items.q: Which model does Harry seem to favour?
options: Anchored flexibility — a couple of required days plus freedom
Fully flexible with no required days
items.why: Inferência: ele descreve prós e contras dos dois primeiros e apresenta o terceiro como o equilíbrio.

items.q: When Harry says "we've taken their evenings," he is warning that…
options: the office should stay open late
employees should work in the evenings
remote work without boundaries can erode people's personal time
items.why: Inferência: "always on" sem limites transforma flexibilidade em disponibilidade permanente.

items.q: How would you best describe Harry's overall message?
options: Attendance should be the main goal
Protect some in-person time on purpose, but respect boundaries
items.why: "protect a little in-person time on purpose, but don't turn attendance into the goal… set boundaries".

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Our developers work asynchronous hours across three continents." Asynchronous work means…
options: work done only in the office
everyone works at the same fixed time
people work at different times, not simultaneously
items.why: Asynchronous = assíncrono: cada um trabalha no seu horário, sem estar online ao mesmo tempo.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "When a manager is in London and the team is in São Paulo, the ___ makes real-time meetings difficult."
items.why: Time zone = fuso horário, o que dificulta reuniões em tempo real.

items.q: "Good managers protect their team's boundaries." Boundaries here means…
options: the lines between work and personal life
items.why: Boundaries = limites entre trabalho e descanso, essenciais para evitar burnout.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "We keep two office days so the team doesn't lose its ___ — the coffee chats and hallway ideas."
items.why: Informal interaction = interação informal, as conversas espontâneas que se perdem no totalmente remoto.

items.q: Someone who is always on is…
items.why: Always on = sempre disponível, nunca desligado do trabalho — o oposto de disconnect.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em conversas sobre políticas de trabalho híbrido. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "HR still has to sign off on the new hybrid policy." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We'll roll out the anchor-days policy team by team." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva.

items.q: "Several employees pushed back on the two fixed office days." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar de algo.

items.q: "It's hard to switch off when your laptop is on the kitchen table." To switch off means to…
options: stop thinking about and doing work
items.why: Switch off = desligar-se do trabalho, desconectar — ligado a boundaries e disconnect.

items.q: "A one-size-fits-all rule won't move the needle on engagement." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível; aqui, negado — não fará diferença.
